title: Rainforests
examples: What is the difference between the canopy and the understorey?
Can you name some animals that live in the rainforest?
Why is biodiversity important in rainforests?

explain.say: Rainforests have many layers, like a tall cake.

draw.text: Forest Layers: Emergent, Canopy, Understorey, Floor

explain.say: The emergent layer is the very top, reaching high into the sky.
Next is the canopy, where most of the leaves and branches live.

draw.text: Canopy: Layer of leaves and branches

explain.say: Below the canopy is the understorey, with smaller plants and bushes growing.
The forest floor is the ground level, where sunlight reaches the soil.
Rainforests have amazing biodiversity, meaning many different life forms.

faq.q: What is the canopy layer exactly?
faq.a: The canopy is the layer formed by the tops of the trees and plants. It catches much of the sunlight.
asks: Where do the leaves mostly live?

faq.q: Are all the layers the same in every rainforest?
faq.a: No, the layers can change depending on the type of rainforest. Some might have fewer visible layers.
asks: Do rainforest layers always look the same?

faq.q: Why is biodiversity so important there?
faq.a: High biodiversity means many different species live together. This keeps the whole ecosystem healthy and balanced.
asks: What does biodiversity mean for rainforests?
Why do we need so many different plants and animals?

faq.q: What lives on the forest floor?
faq.a: On the forest floor, you find things that like low light, like certain types of fungi and small plants.
asks: What is on the ground in a rainforest?
What grows on the forest floor?

faq.q: Does the emergent layer always have the tallest trees?
faq.a: Yes, the emergent layer is home to the tallest trees in the entire forest. They reach far above the rest.
asks: Which layer has the biggest trees?
What is the highest part of the rainforest?

facts: Rainforests have distinct vertical layers, from ground to sky.
The canopy layer is crucial because it intercepts most of the sunlight.
Biodiversity refers to the variety of life in an area.
The forest floor receives very little direct sunlight.

quiz.say: Which layer is the very top, catching the most sunlight?
quiz.why: The emergent layer consists of the tallest trees, placing it at the highest point.

wrong.1: The canopy is below the emergent layer, though it is also high up.
wrong.2: The understorey is a lower layer, beneath the main canopy.
wrong.3: The floor is the ground level, far from the direct sunlight.

quiz.say: If a plant needs lots of light, where would it likely grow?
quiz.why: The canopy is where the main leaves are grouped, catching the most light.

wrong.0: The understorey grows in the shade, below the main leaf layer.
wrong.1: The floor is the darkest area, receiving the least amount of light.
wrong.3: While tall, the canopy describes the main leaf layer, not just the single tallest tree.

quiz.say: A rainforest with many different types of plants and animals shows high:
quiz.why: Biodiversity is the scientific word for the variety of life found in an ecosystem.

wrong.1: Canopy describes a physical layer, not the variety of life.
wrong.2: Ecosystem is the whole system, but biodiversity describes the variety within it.
wrong.3: Habitat is where an organism lives, but biodiversity is about the number of different life forms.
